question: do any 2008 gen1 flight lines run perpendicular to the N-S pattern (a QA tie line), and is there any second-neighbour swath overlap?

inputs.role: raw 2008 MN DNR gen1 LAZ tile, vendor classification, point_source_id = flight line

params.name: nadir_deg
params.why: |scan_angle_rank| <= 1 deg selects returns under the aircraft; the track-fit method of analysis/ELBAEXT2_SCOPE.md Sec 2

params.name: ref_northing
params.why: the northing at which ELBAEXT2_SCOPE.md Sec 2 reports every track easting

params.name: chunk
params.why: points per streamed read; a memory ceiling only -- it changes no result, and the sufficient statistics are exact regardless of how the file is split

columns.tile: gen1 LAZ tile the line was measured in
columns.n: returns of that line in that tile
columns.n_nadir: returns with |scan_angle_rank| <= 1 deg, used for the track fit
columns.heading: compass bearing of the fitted nadir ground track, degrees
columns.speed: along-track speed of the fitted track, m/s
columns.x_ref: easting where the fitted track crosses N 4 884 126, m (UTM 15N)
columns.halfwidth: 99.5th percentile of |cross-track distance| over all that line's returns in the tile, m
columns.amax: maximum |scan_angle_rank| of that line in the tile, degrees
columns.t0: minimum gps_time of that line in the tile, GPS seconds of week
columns.t1: maximum gps_time of that line in the tile, GPS seconds of week
columns.dx_span: easting span of that line's returns in the tile, m
columns.dy_span: northing span of that line's returns in the tile, m
columns.count: returns carrying that classification, summed over all tiles read
columns.psid_a: lower-numbered flight line of the pair
columns.psid_b: higher-numbered flight line of the pair
columns.gap: psid_b - psid_a, i.e. 1 = adjacent, 2 = second neighbour
columns.hw_sum: halfwidth(a) + halfwidth(b), the separation at which the swaths just touch, m
columns.sidelap: hw_sum - spacing: positive = the two swaths overlap by that width, m

headline: flight-line inventory: headings, spacings, second-neighbour overlap, water
